card.name: Opioid equivalence and conversion terms
card.fires_on: The end of the words 'equianalgesic' and 'equivalents' (or 'Equivalent') in opioid dose-conversion text, such as morphine equivalents and equianalgesic doses.

modes.label: Equianalgesic ending
modes.description: The last piece of 'equianalgesic' just before the word 'dose' or 'doses'.
modes.example: daily opioid doses up to 80 mg/day of oral morphine or an equianalges<<ic>> dose of another opioid.

modes.label: Equivalent(s) after morphine or opioid
modes.description: The word 'equivalents' or part of it after morphine or opioid, in dose-conversion phrases.
modes.example: Expressed as Oral Morphine Sulfate Equ<<ival>>ents Prior Daily Dose of Opi

card.writes: It pushes toward words about potency and equivalents, as in dose-equivalence wording.
card.plain: It lights up on opioid dose-conversion wording such as 'equianalgesic' and 'morphine equivalents'.
